Decisive

dih-SY-siv -- stress on the second syllable, SY. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Decisive is able to make decisions quickly and effectively.

A decisive coach, she settled the starting lineup within minutes and never second-guessed her choice.

Worked Example

Smoke begins filling the kitchen, and while everyone else freezes, the manager immediately orders the evacuation, shuts off the gas line, and calls the fire department.

Sizing up a situation and committing to effective action without dithering is what it means to be decisive. It is about the speed and quality of decisions -- not about being loud, bossy, or forceful with people.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

determined: Determined means gripped by a strong, fixed intention to succeed — it describes the drive behind your effort. Decisive describes something narrower: how quickly and effectively you make the choices themselves. A determined climber never gives up; a decisive one picks the route in seconds.

purposeful: Purposeful means acting with a clear aim, so that nothing you do is aimless or accidental. Decisive is specifically about the moment of choosing — sizing up the options fast and committing well. A purposeful routine has direction; a decisive leader settles hard questions quickly.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indecisive: unable to make decisions promptly

hesitant: pausing or holding back in uncertainty

Where it sits · how swiftly and surely choices get made — firm → decisive → resolute

firm vs. decisive: Firm is quieter and more general than decisive -- a firm person holds steady once a position is taken, while a decisive person is distinguished by how quickly and effectively they reach the decision in the first place.

resolute vs. decisive: Resolute can sound even more unshakable than decisive: decisive highlights fast, effective choices in the moment, while resolute suggests a deep, settled determination that holds firm over the long haul.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — de-

prefix — de-: off, away (Latin)

root — cis-

root — cis-: to cut (Latin caedere, cisum)

suffix — -ive

suffix — -ive: having the quality of (Latin -ivus)

Put it together

Put it together: Decisive is built from Latin de- ('off') and caedere ('to cut'): to decide is literally to cut off the other options. A decisive person cuts through hesitation cleanly -- one stroke, and the matter is settled.

Root Check

Word Choice

Decisive is about decisions -- made quickly and well. Keep it distinct from 'assertive,' which is about expressing yourself confidently: a quiet person can be highly decisive. It also describes turning points: a decisive victory or a decisive moment is one that settles the outcome.
